newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prosecutors poised to raid Nomura--media reports.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors poised to raid Nomura--media reports.

text.p: Prosecutors plan to search the headquarters of Japan's biggest brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd, as early as Tuesday as part of investigations into its suspected illegal payments to a corporate client, Japanese media reported.
Both the prosecutors' office and Nomura declined to comment on the reports, which were carried by Japan's Kyodo and Jiji news agencies.

The Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), Japan's securities watchdog, has been probing Nomura over its March 6 admission that two of its directors made discretionary deals banned under Japanese law and funnelled profits to a corporate client.
The client has been linked by the Japanese media to corporate racketeers, known in Japan as "sokaiya", who extort money from companies by threatening to disrupt annual shareholder meetings.

If Nomura's deals are found to violate a commercial code banning payoffs to racketeers, legal action could be taken against the firm, at the request of the SESC. The scandal has already led to the resignation of Nomura's president and an internal investigation by the company.
